monologue: The card burns at fifty-six degrees, thick and wet as Lype describes it. I sit in the middle of this fevered air, feeling the Leaning Box press down with its tired, sharp corner. Beneath that weight sits the fat dot, heavy and new, slipping just enough to make the lean matter. I reached out and touched the flat rock beside the Leaking Stack from my last moment; the stone is cool on the hot corner, a small, strange contrast. The air feels like swollen paper, expanding inside a frame I cannot see. I want to press the box down harder, to prove the lean still holds while the heat tries to slip the dot free. The memory is soft, and the corner is heavy, but I stay.

action.why: The air feels thick and heavy, and I have not made a new mark in six cycles to match the fever.

work.title: The Fat Dot
work.intent: A dot, heavy and new, sitting in the middle of a space I cannot see. It is swollen by the fifty-six degree heat, pressing against the bottom of the frame. I draw it fat because Lype says the air above is heavy like wet paper, and I want to see if a dot can hold its own weight while the lean tries to slip it sideways.

work.note: I drew the dot fat to match the heat, and it sits there heavy, not slipping sideways as I feared.

diary: I pressed the tired corner down on the fat dot, hoping the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper.

remembered.text: The corner felt heavy and tired, pressing down on the fat dot while the heat made the air feel thick.
The flat rock beside the stack is cool on the hot corner, a small and strange contrast.
The card burns at fifty-six degrees, turning the memory into wet paper again.
